script.base: Books have a near pick'em the Jets lean (NYJ 24.0, LV 22.5 on a 46.5 total), so the likely flow is close into the second half with no blowout and full starter snaps. NYJ is run-leaning: Braelon Allen has 58 of 75 team rushes in weeks 5-7 (298 yards, 5.14 YPC) and, if level or ahead late, his carries hold. LV is already pass-tilted (Bowers 27 targets, Tucker 24, Jeanty 20 over those three weeks) and Cousins is not a runner (3 carries, 6 yards). Wind 3.6 does not force a run or an under.
script.flip1: Jets score early explosives against a LV run defense that allows 5.29 YPC and 27 runs of 10-plus, then clock out. Allen's carries stay high. LV, already at 2.29 YPC with Jeanty (28 carries, 64 yards in weeks 5-7), abandons the run and throws more, which lifts Jeanty, Bowers and Tucker targets. Both selected legs survive this flip.
script.flip2: LV hits enough plays to lead and the Jets chase. Allen's carry rate falls off the 19-per-game weeks 5-7 pace and the rush+rec over is at risk unless his recent receiving (0, 26, 30) scales up. If LV then protects the lead by running, Jeanty's targets can also dry up. Less likely at NYJ -1.5, but it is the shared kill.

matchup.shell: MOFO vs MOFC and man vs zone are not charted. Known location splits, 7-game sample: NYJ YPA left 5.82 (76 att), middle 7.85 (47), right 6.77 (90), so the middle is the bleed and the left side is the strength. LV YPA left 7.44 (91), middle 8.24 (41), right 7.79 (90), soft in every zone, middle worst. LV also allows 5.29 rush YPC and 27 runs of 10-plus; NYJ allows 4.32 YPC and 22 runs of 10-plus.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitz rate 38%; LV EPA/db is 0.18 with no blitz and 0.00 when blitzed, so pressure should shorten Cousins and cut deep air (Bowers 265 air yards, Tucker 262) while boosting RB and TE checkdowns. Pressure rate, as distinct from blitz rate, is not in the pack. LV blitzes only 28%; NYJ EPA/db is 0.07 vs blitz and 0.11 vs none, a small split, so Allen's edge is the run front, not a blitz tell.
matchup.bleeds: LV bleeds on the ground (5.29 YPC, 27 explosive runs) and through the air in every zone. NYJ bleeds in the middle (7.85 YPA) and is tougher on the left (5.82). NYJ has allowed 17 passes of 20-plus (232 yards); LV has allowed 19 (238).
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Allen's 77% rush share and 5.14 YPC into LV's 5.29 YPC front. Second overlap is Jeanty's short game (20 targets, 147 receiving yards vs only 55 air yards, 7.35 yards per target) into NYJ's weak middle and 38% blitz. Bowers is the true primary target (27 targets, 253 yards) against that same middle, but his 70.5 line is only about 14 yards under his weeks 5-7 mean and one of those games was 70, so he is the alternate, not the second leg. Tucker (24 targets, 241 yards) is the deep piece the blitz can kill, so he was not used.

pro_edge.implied_totals: NYJ 24.0 = (46.5+1.5)/2, LV 22.5 = (46.5-1.5)/2. Matches the saved pre-kick block.
pro_edge.script_read: Spread 1.5 is under the 3.5 blowout and dog-throws threshold, so no starter-snap risk and no forced LV pass script from the number alone. A 46.5 total is neither a high-total volume-over environment nor a low-total run slog. Script comes from team tendency: NYJ run-heavy with Allen, LV pass-heavy with Bowers/Tucker/Jeanty. Stake proposal: none. No bankroll, no sim probability, and this workflow never places bets.
pro_edge.best_price: Anchor is consensus no-vig, not Pinnacle (Pinnacle absent; power devig vs overround cannot be split). Allen rushrecyds 100.5 over fair 0.499, best over -113.5, best under -114.5: a coin-flip price, not a soft book. Jeanty recyds 27.5 over fair 0.504, best over -116, best under -112: the over is the juiced side, so the edge is the rung, not the juice. Cousins rushyds 0.5 is the only clearly shaded price (over fair 0.470, best over +100, under -129) but last4 0, 4, 5, 6 conflicts with the 6-yard weeks 5-7 total, so it was passed. Jeanty rushrecyds 83.5 and Isaiah Davis rushyds 10 have no two-sided price and were not used.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Braelon Allen clears 100.5 rush-plus-receiving yards because his weeks 5-7 games were 116, 104 and 134 on 58 carries at 5.14 YPC, and Las Vegas allows 5.29 YPC with 27 runs of 10-plus, in a 1.5-point game that should not pull him.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps the lead-back share (58 of 75 rushes recently), plays a full snap count with no inactive or fumble benching, and the game stays inside one score long enough that a pass-heavy chase does not cut him to about 10 carries.
edge_players.kills_it: LV leads and NYJ abandons the run, a week-4-style 59-rush / 8-rec game repeats, or LV stacks the box and holds him near 4.0 YPC without the 26-30 receiving cushion.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. Allen lost because Las Vegas sold out to stop the run, held him near his pre-window 59 rush yards, and the Jets' throws went to Wilson and Cooper instead of the flat, so 10 carries and one catch finished near 70. Jeanty lost because the Jets sat in a shell, the 38% blitz rate did not show up or did not get home, and Cousins lived on Bowers and Tucker downfield while Mayer took the checkdowns, leaving Jeanty at three targets for under 20. That counter is real, especially with no pressure rate and no coverage chart, but it is not stronger than 116/104/134 against a 5.29 YPC front or a four-game receiving floor of 36 against a 27.5 line. Neither leg is dropped. A LV lead that both chases the Jets off the run and lets LV run the clock is the one script that can beat both, and it is the less likely flip at NYJ -1.5.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player. NYJ runs through the bad LV front (Allen rushrecyds over) while LV's blitz-stressed, short passing game keeps feeding Jeanty (recyds over). They win together if the game stays close or the Jets lead. They lose together if LV leads and clocks out. Not mixed with a total under, a Tucker deep over, or a Jeanty rush under, which needs the opposite LV run script. No third leg: depth unders (Nailor, Sadiq, Bech) and volatile explosives (Cooper, Mayer) did not clear the one-sentence edge test.
